Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

rebelrebel 2026.11.10.3

  • A click shows the feature’s row as a table: the tiles carry the row’s number and title only, and the server answers /row/<layer>/<n> with the columns popup names (2-3 ms a click); a bundle writes a layer’s rows beside its tiles, up to 2 million values. Whole numbers as they are, fractions to six significant digits in the page’s language, yes and no, a dash where missing; a web address a link, a picture’s address the picture, a video’s a link.
  • labels and codes in every layer function: a column’s name, unit and description, and a coded column’s labels, by default from the data (a data frame’s label and units attributes, or a parquet file’s own dictionary in data-dict.tidyverse.org’s format).
  • rr_path() takes a number as its order (a sequence, a distance along a transect) as well as a time.

rebelrebel 2026.11.10.2

  • The layer functions, built with the pipe: rr_point(), rr_path() (rows joined in time, a line per group, one column or several), rr_line(), rr_segment() (a line from each row’s start to its end), rr_polygon() and rr_text(), one internal function for all. They take their arguments in one order and words (colour, fill, size, linewidth, opacity, label; palette, limits, stretch, legend; popup, hover, choose; name, info, section, visible; minzoom, maxzoom). A bare name is a column, a string a value.
  • rr_map(data) starts a map the layer functions add to; choose names the columns the reader picks, sections the sidebar’s boxes. A layer function given data first starts a map. Data are a parquet file, folder or glob, a lazy DuckDB table, a data frame or an sf object.
  • Colours from the data: Okabe-Ito for up to eight values, Paired for up to twelve, Glasbey’s 32 beyond, the rest grey as “other”; viridis for ordered factors, numbers, dates and times (over the 1st to 99th percentile, or limits, stretched linearly, on a log scale or in equal shares). palette overrides them: a name written loosely, colours, colours by value, or a function of n.
  • The time panel is generic: rr_time() takes its columns (col, no default) and its group (by) from the call or from the map (a path’s group and time); interval tables are read by start and end, or as named; the page names the group’s list by its column and counts rows. Points carry their time and group for it.
  • The quick look at vessels’ pings and tracks is no longer here: it is ramb’s, as wrappers over these functions.

rebelrebel 2026.11.10.1

  • The base maps are those that show the sea floor: EMODnet’s sea floor (its 2020 base layer), the first and the one a map opens on; the same darkened (emodnet_dark); EMODnet’s lighter atlas (v12); and Esri’s ocean, which reaches beyond Europe’s seas; and none. Carto’s Positron, Voyager and Dark Matter (a flat sea) and Esri’s satellite tiles are no longer offered. Each picture has a Carto style’s place and sea names drawn over it (Positron’s, or Dark Matter’s on the dark one), which also give the layers’ own labels their fonts: a base map’s labels, label_layers, paint and background in rr_basemaps(). The page opens on a picture base map.

rebelrebel 2026.11.10

  • The package starts as ramb’s map viewer, moved here unchanged but for its names: rb_map() is rr_map(), rb_map_layer() rr_layer(), rb_map_group() rr_section(), rb_map_serve() and rb_map_stop() rr_serve() and rr_stop(), rb_map_bundle() rr_bundle(), the tile makers rr_tiles_table(), rr_tiles_dem() and rr_tiles_mbtiles(), rr_palettes(), rr_basemaps(), rr_notes(), rr_notes_add(), rr_verdicts() and rr_time(); ramb’s rb_read_example() is rr_example(), with five of ramb’s datasets (dansk, dansk_harbours, dansk_relief, trawlsurvey, trawlsurveytows). rb_map_pings() and rb_map_track() are internal until rr_point() and rr_path() take their place.
  • The page’s libraries are in the package (inst/engine/vendor): MapLibre GL JS 5.24.0, maplibre-contour 0.1.1 and uPlot 1.6.30, served by rr_serve() at /vendor/ and copied into a bundle’s vendor folder, so a map draws with no network but the base map’s.
